vedic_reference.note: Prahalada was a devotee of Lord Vishnu and is famous for his unwavering devotion. He is the son of King Hiranyakashipu and Queen Kayadhu. He was born to fulfill a boon given to Hiranyakashipu by Brahma that he would be killed neither by man nor beast, neither inside nor outside, neither day nor night. Hiranyakashipu tried to kill Prahalada many times but failed each time due to Prahalada's devotion to Lord Vishnu. Eventually, Lord Vishnu himself killed Hiranyakashipu in the form of a man-lion (Narasimha), fulfilling the condition of neither man nor beast.
